label: The first holder could not lack the act by which it holds, from C* in the holding sense (inference)
rule: Contrapose C* in the holding sense at the first holder
meaning: New non-transcription conditional derivation. Given a holder f of x, not held in the act r by which it holds: f is in act in r (actualizer premise), and if f could lack that act, C* in the holding sense would make it held in r, so it could not. This is where the holding route uses C*, and through it concurrent actualization. It is not the pure-act conclusion: f may be in potency or held in other respects (Control part 6), and reaching all-respect unheldness would need a respect-free per se premise, which mutual holding in different respects (part 6) or in one respect (two leaning cards) puts in question. All premises stay OPEN. No premise is established.
